name: Pale Violet-Plumbeous
lede: Pale Violet-Plumbeous is a cool, faintly violet grey whose name joins a color (violet) to *plumbeous*, Latin for lead-colored, one of Ridgway's own qualifying terms.

sections.title: A lead-colored qualifier
sections.body: Ridgway's 1912 color standards record this swatch on plate XLIX, hue 53, tone f [1]. *Plumbeous* is Ridgway's own Latin-derived term for a dull leaden grey, used across his system to qualify a hue rather than to name a material in its own right [1]. ColorHub's library flags the full compound name itself as "obscure, qualified or novelty," which is why it keeps the plainer [[silver]] as the closest everyday match, about 3.7 units of ΔE away [1]. "Violet" here is also a qualifier, not the dominant hue: the swatch reads as a near-neutral grey with only a faint cool cast, washed pale than to any true violet [1]. [[periwinkle]] and [[grey]] sit nearby in the same cool-neutral family [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Pale Violet-Plumbeous in 821 of 23,781 paintings (3.45 percent), as photographed, overwhelmingly as a highlight [2]. It peaks in the 1930s, in 8 of 69 paintings, at more than three times the archive's overall rate, and two of Gustav Klimt's *Beethoven Frieze* panels are among its closest matches [2]. It keeps company with Silver, Periwinkle and Cornflower more than chance [2]. These are screen approximations of aged, varnished canvases, not pigment identifications [2].
